verdict.rationale: Proa documents typed Rust components with compile-time-checked props that can be composed. It also documents local interactive state: adding signals and event handlers emits island JavaScript with seed state. However, the evidence is thin on how state stays encapsulated per component and on composing stateful components into larger UIs. Missing for 10: docs on component-scoped state lifecycle, examples of nesting or composing stateful islands into complex UIs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build encapsulated components that manage their own local state and compose them into complex UIs

citations.quote: Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state
